answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in an AI agent economy, the network uses Silicon PUF staking. Each agent must lock a cryptographic ember derived from its unique silicon physical unclonable function. The protocol verifies this via a zero-knowledge karst proof, ensuring the hardware is unique without exposing the PUF. If an agent acts maliciously, the cipher key is slashed. An attacker must purchase distinct physical chips for each fake identity, making mass deployment economically unviable due to high hardware procurement costs.
